newsitem.title: IRAN: Khatami confirmed as Iran's president.
newsitem.headline: Khatami confirmed as Iran's president.

text.p: Mohammad Khatami, a Shi'ite Moslem clergyman known for his moderate political views, took over as Iran's new president on Sunday and said the Islamic republic sought friendly relations with all countries.
Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who has authority over the presidency and all other institutions of the revolutionary government, confirmed Khatami in office.

Khatami succeeded Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani, president since 1989. He is due to be formally sworn in on Monday at the conservative-dominated parliament, whose speaker he defeated by a landslide in May presidential election.
Khatami, 54, said Iran pursued peace and security in the world despite the expansionist policies of the big powers which it considered the main obstacle to world peace.
Iran was keen to form brotherly relations with all countries and nations based on its national interests and revolutionary ideals, he said.
He called for cooperation of the legislative and judicial branches of government and the supreme leader's continued support to enable the new government to carry out its responsibilities.

Khamenei, a conservative like most of the Iranian political establishment, said in a decree read by Rafsanjani that Khatami's presidency opened a new chapter in a healthy, tranquil atmosphere filled with the spirit of cooperation and harmony.

"This comes at a time when many nations in different parts of the world are engaged in bloody confrontations and crises and are suffering under tyrant regimes or are being exploited in materialistic party politics," Khamenei's decree said.

The supreme leader said the presidential election in May was orderly and had dealt another blow to enemies who worked to dissuade the nation from taking part in the elections and distance it from its political leadership.

"Now once again the grave responsibility of heading the executive power is put on the shoulders of an experienced and revolutionary clergyman, a man of letters and culture who has been trained in a seminary," Khamenei said.
He said this was proof that genuine spiritual values and full commitment to religion and ethics had been and would continue to be of paramount importance.

Khamenei's decree said his confirmation of Khatami as well as the vote of the nation remained valid as long as the president followed the divine teachings of Islam to defend the oppressed against the forces of arrogance and oppression.
Khatami's takeover was closely watched by the millions of Iranians who gave him his surprise landslide victory.
A broad coalition of discontented youth, middle classes and women who handed him the presidency are eager to see him take on conservatives and introduce economic and social reforms.
Khatami has yet to announce his cabinet which requires approval by the 270-member parliament headed by his defeated election opponent, Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri.
